title: Approve a workforce work entry and verify the saved result
summary: Create a separate standby-hours example, save it unapproved, select and save approval, verify the returned row after reload, and apply a single-day filter.
prerequisites: Authorized workforce view and management access in a fictional training department.
An existing worker, employment and training establishment.

scenes.title: Find the work-entry approval column
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual work-entry form, approval checkbox, saved row or applied date filter as discussed.
scenes.narration: Open Workforce and choose Work entries. The table separates the worker, hours, hours type, establishment, context and approval status. In this training department, the existing two-hour entry shows No under Approved. We will create a separate example and follow it from an unapproved save to a verified approved result. An administrator needs the appropriate workforce access for these controls. The earlier example remains unchanged.
scenes.practice: Identify the Approved column and choose a separate fictional entry for practice.

scenes.title: Prepare a separate standby entry
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual work-entry form, approval checkbox, saved row or applied date filter as discussed.
scenes.narration: Select Add work entry. In the form, the worker is Matthew Casey. Set Date to November first, twenty twenty-six, enter one point two five Hours, and choose Standby under Hours type. Select the training establishment appropriate to the example. These fields describe this individual work entry. Check the worker, date, quantity and hours type together before continuing, so the approval will refer to the intended row.
scenes.practice: Prepare a fictional worker, date, hours quantity, hours type and establishment.

scenes.title: Save the entry with approval clear
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual work-entry form, approval checkbox, saved row or applied date filter as discussed.
scenes.narration: Scroll to the bottom of the form. External source and External id provide references for this example. Leave the Approved checkbox clear for the first save. The Approved payroll cost field is also blank in this exercise. Select Save, then find the new row with the context TRAINING ONLY, Approval exercise. Its date, one point two five hours and Standby type are visible, and Approved still reads No. This returned row confirms the initial saved state.
scenes.practice: Save the example unapproved and verify the returned row instead of relying only on the form.

scenes.title: Select approval for the intended row
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual work-entry form, approval checkbox, saved row or applied date filter as discussed.
scenes.narration: Use the pencil control at the right of the new exercise row to reopen it. Scroll to Approved and select the checkbox. In this view, the table on the left still shows the earlier saved value, No, while the form checkbox on the right is selected. The form change still needs to be saved. Confirm that this is the intended training entry, then select Save to store its approval status.
scenes.practice: Reopen the correct row, select Approved, and save the change.

scenes.title: Reload and compare the saved result
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual work-entry form, approval checkbox, saved row or applied date filter as discussed.
scenes.narration: Reload the Work entries page. The new exercise row now shows Yes under Approved. The worker, date, one point two five hours and Standby type remain visible on that same row. The earlier two-hour entry still shows No. Compare the complete row when reviewing an approval, rather than reading a Yes value without its worker and date. The Approved payroll cost column remains blank for this software exercise.
scenes.practice: Reload and verify that the intended row changed to Yes while the earlier entry stayed No.

scenes.title: Filter to the work date
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual work-entry form, approval checkbox, saved row or applied date filter as discussed.
scenes.narration: Use the two date fields above the table to focus the review. Set both boundaries to November first, twenty twenty-six, then select Filter. The returned table contains the single exercise entry for that date, including its Standby hours, context and Yes approval value. Changing the date fields alone does not refresh this table; the Filter button applies the selected range. Check those boundaries when a saved entry seems to be missing from the list.
scenes.practice: Apply a single-day range and verify the matching entry in the returned table.

scenes.title: Use consistent review responsibilities
scenes.capture_intent: Show the actual work-entry form, approval checkbox, saved row or applied date filter as discussed.
scenes.narration: This workflow gives a department a visible saved approval status for a particular work entry. A security supervisor can review patrol standby time, a search-and-rescue coordinator can review an exercise entry, and a community paramedicine or mental health response team can review its recorded work. Wildland contractors, industrial response teams, and fire and E M S departments can use the same worker, date, hours type and context checks. Agree who reviews entries, then verify the saved result in the appropriate date range.
scenes.practice: Define who reviews entries for your department and which row details they must check.

sector_examples.scenario: Review the worker, date, hours type and context of a patrol standby entry.
Use a training entry to practice supervisor review without changing the earlier example.
Review work-entry details for a community paramedicine or mental health response team.
Apply a consistent date and context review to contractor work entries.
Compare work-entry approval with the recorded worker, quantity and context.
Verify the saved approval of a department standby-hours exercise.

scope_limits: Source proposal only; generated speech, complete listening, caption correspondence, actual encoded frames and live playback remain required.
Only one fictional entry is created and its approval flag changed. No payroll amount, compensation profile, cost run, payroll payment, annual report or external integration is demonstrated.
The earlier two-hour entry is preserved. External reference inputs are clipped in the narrow form and their complete values are not narrated as readable.
